intro: Growing startups do not fail FinOps because they skipped a multi-cloud strategy. They fail because staging clones production, logs are on debug, and the bill lands on a founder’s card.

We will not invent a savings percentage. We map tags, idle resources, and an owner. Then you decide whether a FinOps consulting engagement is worth it. Book: Discovery $99. AI-specific spend: AI FinOps.

The first dashboard you need is not a FinOps platform. It is the native bill grouped by service and tag, exported to a sheet the founder actually opens. Fancy allocation comes after that habit exists.

sections.h2: The first week, not the first framework
paras: Turn on tags. Kill unattached disks and leftover load balancers. Right-size the one always-on GPU nobody uses after the demo. Put a budget alert on the account that actually pays.
bullets: One billing account owner with a deputy.
Non-prod sleeps. Prod does not share the same unrestricted key as CI.
Logs: keep what you query. Debug is not an architecture.

paras: Reserved instances and savings plans punish you if the footprint is still changing every sprint. Get the shape stable, then commit. Startups that buy three-year RIs in month four usually pay twice.

sections.h2: Engineering guardrails that do not block deploys
paras: A cost check in CI that fails on a new untagged resource is cheaper than a monthly shame meeting. Autoscaling without a max is a blank check. Preview environments need TTLs.
If the bill is now material to runway and nobody can explain last month’s spike, map it in Discovery. Implementation is scoped. Plans: /plans/.

The first dashboard you need is not a FinOps platform. It is the native bill grouped by service and tag, exported to a sheet the founder actually opens. Fancy allocation comes after that habit exists.
CI that builds a full production-shaped stack on every pull request is a classic leak. Cache images. TTL the preview. Fail the pipeline if a resource has no owner tag.
GPU demos left on over the weekend are still the funniest line item we see. Calendar a shutdown. Treat “I’ll turn it off later” as a production incident waiting for a weekend.

sections.h2: How to use this guide in Discovery
paras: If you arrived on this page for “cloud cost optimization for growing startups”, the next step is not a platform RFP. Name the queue, the tool that would hurt if an agent wrote to it, and the person who can disable the flow. Bring those three to Discovery at $99.

faqs.q: Should we multi-cloud to save money?
faqs.a: Usually no. Two clouds without tags is two messy bills. Optimize the one you are on until a real constraint (region, customer, GPU availability) forces the second.
No. Guarantees without seeing idle resources, log volume, and commitments are marketing. We map the waste, then you choose what to turn off.

faqs.q: Does Discovery include a full FinOps practice?
faqs.a: No. It is a 30-minute map plus written follow-up. A practice is a later retainer if you want one.

cta.p: Bring last month’s invoice. We name the idle, the logs, and the owner.
